title: Reading practice: Which Bike Rental Is the Better Deal?
description: Eight reading items about a math problem that compares two rental prices and a table of after-school help sessions, practicing explaining math reasoning and finding information in a schedule.

stimuli.title: Which Bike Rental Is the Better Deal?
paragraphs: The Green Valley Student Council is planning a bike trip for its volunteers, and each rider will rent a bike for a few hours. Two shops offer different prices. Company A charges a flat fee of $6 for each rental plus $2 for every hour. Company B has no flat fee, but it charges $3 for every hour.

Before the trip, Kofi told the council, “Company A is cheaper because its hourly price is lower, $2 compared with $3.” Lena disagreed. “The hourly price is only part of the cost,” she said. “We also have to include the flat fee.” To check Kofi’s claim, Lena decided to find the total cost of a 4-hour rental at each company.

First, she calculated Company A’s total: 4 hours times $2 equals $8, and $8 plus the $6 fee equals $14. Next, she calculated Company B’s total: 4 hours times $3 equals $12. Because $12 is less than $14, Lena concluded that Company B is cheaper for a 4-hour rental. However, she noticed that the difference between the two companies changes with the number of hours. When she tried a 6-hour rental, both companies cost $18. When she tried an 8-hour rental, Company A cost $22 and Company B cost $24.

Lena summarized her findings for the council: “Neither company is always cheaper. For rentals shorter than 6 hours, Company B costs less. For rentals longer than 6 hours, Company A costs less. Our volunteers plan to ride for 3 hours, so Company B is the better choice.”

stimuli.title: After-School Help Sessions
stimuli.caption: When and where students can get help from teachers after school. Every session starts at 3:15 p.m.

items.stem: Why does Lena say that the hourly price is “only part of the cost”?

options.text: Company B also charges a flat fee that Kofi forgot to include.
The hourly price changes during a rental, so Kofi’s numbers are wrong.
Company A also charges a flat fee of $6 for each bike rental.
The council pays for part of each rental, so the prices are lower.

distractors.a: Company B has no flat fee. Company A is the shop that charges one.
distractors.b: The passage never says the price changes. The rate stays $2 or $3 for every hour.
distractors.d: The passage does not say the council pays for any part of the rental.

items.explanation: Company A charges $6 for each rental plus $2 for every hour, so comparing only the hourly prices leaves out part of the cost.

support.clue: Reread the first paragraph and compare how each company charges.
support.frame: The hourly price is not the whole cost because ______.
support.model: Mentor example (a different cost). “Plan X costs $20 a month and includes 5 GB of data. Plan Y costs $12 a month and charges $3 for each GB. To compare the plans, a family adds up everything it would pay in one month.” Find what is missing from Kofi’s comparison in the same way.

misconceptions.b: adds a changing rate that is not stated
misconceptions.d: adds a detail that is not in the text

facts: Company A: $6 flat fee plus $2 per hour. Company B: $3 per hour with no flat fee.

items.stem: Put Lena’s steps for checking Kofi’s claim in order.

items.text: She tried 6 hours and 8 hours and found that the cheaper company changes.
She multiplied 4 hours by $2 and added the $6 fee to find Company A’s cost, $14.
She told the council that Company B is the better choice for a 3-hour trip.
She compared $14 with $12 and decided that Company B is cheaper for 4 hours.
She multiplied 4 hours by $3 to find Company B’s cost, $12.

items.explanation: Lena finds Company A’s total, then Company B’s total, compares them, tests other lengths of rental, and finally gives her recommendation.

support.clue: Look for the order words in the third paragraph: First, Next, Because, However. Each one begins a new step. Her recommendation is in the last paragraph.
support.model: Mentor example (a different check). “First, Dara added the prices of three notebooks, $2 + $3 + $4. Next, she compared the total with her $10. Because $9 is less than $10, she decided she could buy them.” Steps in a check follow a logical order. Order Lena’s steps the same way.

facts: For 6 hours both companies cost $18; for 8 hours Company A costs $22 and Company B costs $24.

items.stem: Choose the words that best complete an explanation of why Kofi’s claim does not always hold.

dropdown.template: Company A has a lower hourly price, but it also has a {1}. For short rentals, that charge makes Company A cost {2} Company B. For long rentals, the lower hourly price {3} the extra charge, so Company A costs less.

items.explanation: The $6 fee is paid once, so it raises Company A’s cost for short rentals (4 hours: $14 compared with $12). After 6 hours, the $2-per-hour rate saves enough to make up for the fee.

support.clue: Think about what happens to each company’s total as the hours increase. The flat fee is paid once, while the hourly price is paid again for every hour.
support.frame: A charge that is paid once is different from a charge that is paid each ______.
support.model: Mentor example (a different comparison). “A gym costs $20 to join plus $5 per visit, while a day pass costs $9 per visit. For a few visits, the day pass costs less because the joining fee is paid at the start. For many visits, the lower price per visit catches up with the joining fee.” Use the same reasoning about the rental fee.

facts: Company A total = 6 + 2h and Company B total = 3h; they are equal at h = 6 (both $18).
For h less than 6, Company B costs less; for h greater than 6, Company A costs less.

items.stem: Match each part of the discussion to what the speaker says.

right.text: The flat fee must also be included in the cost.
Company B is the better choice for 3 hours.
Its hourly price is lower, $2 compared with $3.

items.explanation: Kofi claims Company A is cheaper and gives the hourly price as his reason. Lena objects that the flat fee must be included and recommends Company B for a 3-hour trip.

support.clue: Find Kofi’s words in the second paragraph, inside quotation marks. Then find Lena’s reply, which includes the word “also,” and her summary in the last paragraph.
support.frame: Kofi claims that ______ because ______. Lena replies that ______.
support.model: Mentor example (a different discussion). Ana says, “The blue backpack is better because it is cheaper.” Eli says, “It is cheaper, but it has no zipper pocket, which we need.” Ana’s claim is that blue is better, and her reason is the price. Eli’s objection is the missing pocket. Match the speakers’ ideas in the same way.

facts: The bike rental scenario is fictional.

items.stem: Lena speaks to the council. Put these sentences in the order she would say them: first her claim, then the evidence, and last her conclusion.

items.text: Next, at Company B, 3 hours cost 3 times $3, which is $9.
Because $9 is less than $12, each rider saves $3 with Company B.
Company B is the better choice for our 3-hour trip.
First, at Company A, 3 hours cost $6 plus 3 times $2, which is $12.

items.explanation: A strong argument states the claim first, gives the evidence for Company A and then for Company B, and ends with a conclusion that compares the totals.

support.clue: Look for the order words in the sentences, and notice which sentence compares the two totals.
support.frame: My claim is ______. The evidence is ______. Because ______, I conclude ______.
support.model: Mentor example (a different argument). “Our class should take the earlier train. The earlier train takes 40 minutes, and the later train takes 55 minutes. Because 40 is less than 55, the earlier train saves 15 minutes.” Notice the claim, the evidence, and the conclusion. Order the sentences about the rentals the same way.

items.stem: Use the prices in the passage. Sort each rental length: which company costs less?
items.explanation: Company B costs less for rentals shorter than 6 hours (2 hours: $6 compared with $10; 5 hours: $15 compared with $16; 4 hours: $12 compared with $14). Company A costs less for rentals longer than 6 hours (8 hours: $22 compared with $24; 10 hours: $26 compared with $30).

support.clue: Look at Lena’s summary in the last paragraph. Compare each rental length with 6 hours. You can check your choice by finding each company’s total.
support.frame: Because ___ hours is ______ than 6 hours, Company ___ costs less.
support.model: Mentor example (a different rule). “A monthly bus pass is cheaper than single tickets for any month with more than 4 rides.” For 6 rides, the pass is cheaper, and for 3 rides it is not. Compare each number with the rule’s cutoff. Sort the rental lengths with Lena’s cutoff in the same way.

facts: Company A total = 6 + 2h; Company B total = 3h. At h = 2: $10 and $6. At h = 4: $14 and $12. At h = 5: $16 and $15. At h = 8: $22 and $24. At h = 10: $26 and $30.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the help sessions are true?

options.text: Reading and writing help is offered on Monday.
The Wednesday session lasts longer than the other sessions.
Sessions end at 4:00 p.m. every day.
Students can get help from Mr. Chen in the computer lab.

distractors.a: Monday is math help in Room 112. Reading and writing help is on Tuesday.
distractors.c: Wednesday’s session ends at 4:15 p.m., and Friday has no session at all.

items.explanation: Every session starts at 3:15 p.m. and Wednesday’s ends at 4:15 p.m., an hour long, while the others end at 4:00 p.m. Mr. Chen helps in the computer lab on Thursday.

support.clue: Put a finger on each row. Check the Ends at column for every day and compare it with the starting time in the caption.
support.frame: On ______, students can get help with ______ in ______.
support.model: Mentor example (a different schedule). A club table shows Monday: Chess, Room 3 and Tuesday: Art, Room 9. We read it as, “On Tuesday, students can do art in Room 9.” Read across one row to say a true sentence. Check each choice against its row.

facts: From 3:15 p.m., a session ending at 4:15 p.m. lasts 60 minutes and one ending at 4:00 p.m. lasts 45 minutes.

items.stem: Match each student to the help session that fits.

left.text: Beatriz wants help writing a reading response.
Joon has a question about his science experiment.
Dara needs help using a spreadsheet program on a computer.

items.explanation: Fractions are math help on Monday, a reading response is reading and writing help on Tuesday, a science experiment question is science help on Wednesday, and using a spreadsheet program is computer help on Thursday.

support.clue: Find the kind of help in the second column first. Then slide your finger to the day and place in the same row.
support.frame: ______ needs ______ help, so ______ should go on ______.
support.model: Mentor example (a different schedule). A pool schedule lists Monday: Beginners, Lane 1 and Tuesday: Racing, Lane 4. A new swimmer who needs to learn to float matches Monday, Lane 1. Match the need to the kind of help, then read across the row.
